turns.text: hi! i need help understanding wake windows. theo is 2 months old (born july 19) and right now he naps on demand, mostly on my chest, which is exactly why i want an actual schedule. could you explain how wake windows work and put it in table form? columns for age, wake window and number of naps please. i think better in tables 🙃

Happy to. A wake window is the stretch of time a baby can comfortably stay awake between sleeps. Past that point they get overtired, which paradoxically makes naps shorter and harder. Younger babies have short windows that lengthen as their sleep matures.

Typical ranges (every baby varies, so treat these as starting points):

| Age | Wake window | Naps per day |
|---|---|---|
| 0-4 weeks | 35-60 min | 5-8 |
| 1-2 months | 45-75 min | 4-6 |
| 2-3 months | 60-90 min | 4-5 |
| 3-4 months | 75-120 min | 3-5 |
| 4-6 months | 90-150 min | 3-4 |
| 6-9 months | 2-3 hrs | 2-3 |

Since Theo is 2 months old, aim for roughly 60-90 minutes awake, which includes feeding and diaper time. Watch for sleepy cues (yawning, staring off, red eyebrows, fussing) and start the nap routine when you see them, not after.

To move away from contact naps, put him down drowsy but awake for at least some of them, and keep the same short wind-down each time. Does that fit with the timing you're picturing?

yes, that helps. ok so here's my real day. this morning was our second boardwalk walk with the stroller and it came to 40 minutes again, he dozed off halfway. can you fit that into a sample nap table with actual clock times? wake up around 7. also he's on my chest right now and i just placed three jigsaw pieces one-handed, so that's the level of productivity we're at

Three pieces one-handed counts as a win. Here's a sample day with a 7:00 wake-up, using about 75-minute wake windows and treating the 40-minute stroller walk as a nap-friendly activity:

| Block | Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Wake + feed | 7:00 | Diaper, feed, a little play |
| Stroller walk | 8:15-8:55 | Let him doze if he's sleepy; this counts as nap 1 |
| Awake | 8:55-10:15 | Feed, floor time |
| Nap 2 (crib, drowsy) | 10:15-11:45 | Try the crib here |
| Awake | 11:45-1:00 | Feed, diaper |
| Nap 3 | 1:00-2:15 | Crib or contact, whichever works |
| Awake | 2:15-3:30 | Play, feed |
| Nap 4 | 3:30-4:30 | Shorter, so evening isn't pushed late |
| Awake + feeds | 4:30-6:15 | The fussy stretch; a short catnap is fine |
| Catnap | 6:15-6:45 | Optional |
| Bedtime routine | 7:45-8:30 | Bath, feed, dim lights |

Stroller naps can be shorter than crib naps, so if he wakes after 20-30 minutes, just shift the next window earlier. Log the actual times for a few days and adjust. Does the day look workable?

great, this works. can you keep the evening open-ish though, i do baby laundry tonight and the laundry room is card-only so i need a slot where i can actually leave the apartment. thanks, and sorry for typing one-handed

No apology needed. Here's the evening with a clear laundry slot:

| Time | Plan |
|---|---|
| 4:30-6:15 | Awake stretch with feeds; handle fussiness |
| 6:15-6:45 | Catnap (optional) |
| 6:45-7:30 | Awake, feed |
| 7:30-8:30 | Bedtime routine and sleep, so you can head out |

Since the laundry room only takes a card, load it up and keep the card in your pocket. The best time to leave is once he's asleep, as long as someone else is home to listen for him. If you're alone, take the monitor with you and check the range. If it isn't reliable, run the loads while he's in the crib napping at 1:00-2:15 instead, or carry him in a carrier for a quick trip.

Give this a few days and compare the log against the table. Want a blank tracking version?
